part.defensiveMove.title: The defensive move
part.defensiveMove.summary: Before attacking, ask what your opponent threatens and find the move that stops it.
ex.dm.XAlck: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.dm.XAlck.hint: Before choosing a square for the king, see what each way out of check leaves for White.
ex.dm.XAlck.solution: 34...f5! blocks the check with the pawn and attacks the queen on g4. After 35.Rxe4+ Kxd7, the king gets out of check by capturing the rook on d7, and Black is a rook up. With 34...Kf6?, the king is exposed, and White gives mate.
ex.dm.JDu0y: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.dm.JDu0y.hint: Both bishops are attacked. How can you get out of check without losing the time to capture first?
ex.dm.JDu0y.solution: 29...g6! blocks the check with the pawn and attacks the queen on f5. The queen must move, and your bishop captures the one on b2: after 30.Qa5 Bxb2, Black wins a piece. With 29...Kg8?, the bishop on b2 captures your bishop on d4.
ex.dm.AejX5: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.dm.AejX5.hint: A rook can block the check and attack the queen at the same time.
ex.dm.AejX5.solution: 25.Rc2! blocks the check with the rook and attacks the queen on b2, and the bishop on e4 defends the rook. After 25...Qxc2+ 26.Bxc2, White has the queen for a rook. With 25.Kf1?, the king gets out of check, but Black is better.
ex.dm.rwWzZ: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.dm.rwWzZ.hint: What does White threaten if the knight on d4 moves? Look at the diagonal up to h8.
ex.dm.rwWzZ.solution: White threatens 16.Nxe6: the knight leaves d4 and opens the diagonal from the queen on c3 to the rook on h8. 15...Be5! closes that diagonal and attacks the knight on d4, pinned to the queen on c3 and also attacked by your queen on d8. After 16.Bb5+ c6, Black blocks the check, and the knight is still pinned and attacked twice. With 15...Qe7?, White follows with 16.Bb5+ and wins material.
ex.dm.Kw8qU: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.dm.Kw8qU.hint: Your rook on c1 is attacked. Before saving it, see whether some black piece has been left undefended.
ex.dm.Kw8qU.solution: 25.Qxe8+! Before saving the rook on c1, the queen captures with check the rook on e8, which was undefended. After 25...Kh7 26.Rf1, the rook steps out of the attack and defends f2, and White is ahead in material. With 25.Rf1?, Black saves the rook on e8 and keeps the extra knight.
ex.dm.oCw6H: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.dm.oCw6H.hint: Block the check while attacking the queen. Then count its squares.
ex.dm.oCw6H.solution: 21...b5! blocks the check with the pawn and attacks the queen on a4, which is trapped: b3 and c4 belong to the knight on a5, a3 and b4 to the bishop on f8, and b5 to the pawn. After 22.Qxa5 Qxa5, the queen captures the knight and your queen recaptures it: Black wins the queen for a knight. With 21...Nc6?, the knight blocks the check, but the white queen stays free, and the game is level.
ex.dm.p4VPl: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.dm.p4VPl.hint: The white queen has entered your camp. Block the check with a piece that also attacks it.
ex.dm.p4VPl.solution: 36...Rd8! blocks the check with the rook from d2 and attacks the queen on a8, which is trapped: a7, b7 and b8 belong to your queen on c7, a6 to the rook on f6, c8 to the rook on d8, and the diagonal to f3 is watched too: c6 by the queen, d5 by the rook on d8, e4 by the knight and f3 by the rook on f6. After 37.Qxd8+ Qxd8, Black wins the queen for a rook. With 36...Kh7?, the king gets out of check, but the white queen escapes, and the game is level.
part.counterattack.title: Counterattack
part.counterattack.summary: When your opponent threatens, look for a check or a bigger threat that arrives first.
ex.ca.SJ2oi: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.ca.SJ2oi.hint: Before defending h2, look for a check that leads to mate.
ex.ca.SJ2oi.solution: Black threatens 29...Qxh2#. 29.Rxg7+! captures the pawn on g7 with check, and the king only has h5. After 29...Kh5 30.Rg5#, the rook gives mate before the black queen. With 29.Rg8?, Black gives mate on h2.
ex.ca.VPMks: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.ca.VPMks.hint: Black threatens mate. You have a check that opens the way for the queen.
ex.ca.VPMks.solution: Black threatens 26...Qe1#. 26.Rxg7+! gives up the rook with check. After 26...Bxg7 27.Qxg7#, the queen gives mate, defended by the knight on e6. With 26.Nxf8?, the black queen gives mate on e1.
ex.ca.bx46r: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.ca.bx46r.hint: Before defending e8, look at your queen's checks.
ex.ca.bx46r.solution: White threatens 30.Qe8#. 29...Qf2+! gives check, and the king only has h1. After 30.Kh1 Qxg2#, the queen captures the pawn on g2 with mate, defended by the rook on c2. With 29...Rxg2+?, the king captures the rook, and White wins.
ex.ca.s0QIE: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.ca.s0QIE.hint: White threatens mate. You have a check that pulls the white king out of the corner.
ex.ca.s0QIE.solution: White threatens 37.Qh5#. 36...Rxf1+! captures the rook on f1 with check, and the king has to recapture. After 37.Kxf1 Qe1#, the queen gives mate, defended by the rook on e3. With 36...Rxf3?, White gives mate on h5.
ex.ca.9OfQH: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.ca.9OfQH.hint: White threatens mate. Look at the checks you have.
ex.ca.9OfQH.solution: White threatens 42.Qxd8#. 41...Ra8+! brings the rook to the a-file with check. After 42.Qa7 Rxa7#, the rook captures the queen with mate. With 41...Rxd1?, the white queen gives mate on e8.
ex.ca.MRPUm: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.ca.MRPUm.hint: Before defending f2, count the black king's squares.
ex.ca.MRPUm.solution: Black threatens 28...Qxf2#. 28.Qh8+! gives up the queen with check, and the bishop on g7 has to capture it. After 28...Bxh8 29.Rxh8#, the rook gives mate, and the knight on f5 covers e7 and g7. With 28.Nxg7?, the black queen captures the pawn on f2 with mate.
ex.ca.idWDF: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.ca.idWDF.hint: Black threatens mate. Look for a check that captures a piece.
ex.ca.idWDF.solution: Black threatens 33...Qe2#. 33.Qxd5+! captures the knight with check, and the king cannot recapture: the rook on g5 defends d5. After 33...Kb6 34.Qc5#, the queen gives mate, defended by the pawns on b4 and d4. With 33.Rxd5?, Black gives checks and captures your queen on f7.
ex.ca.0w7b1: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.ca.0w7b1.hint: Before stopping the threat, see whether you have a check that wins material.
ex.ca.0w7b1.solution: White threatens 22.Qxh7#. 21...Qxc5+! captures the knight with check before defending. After 22.Kh1 h5, the pawn closes the queen's way to h7, and Black is a piece up. With 21...h5?, you stop the threat, but White saves the knight, and Black loses the advantage.
